turn_text: Welcome to another in our series of special presidential editions of The Washington Health Report. This week we hear from Republican presidential contender Senator John McCain on his plan to reform the nation's health care system in his own words. McCain's proposal differs sharply from those of the Democrats who've taken the lead in making health care reform a priority. McCain says the key to affordable health insurance and more comprehensive insurance coverage is to bring healthcare costs down. He would give individuals tax credits to help pay for health insurance and he would reform Medicare and Medicaid to sharply cut costs. Now, another hallmark in McCain's plan is freedom in the use of healthcare dollars. He would even allow veterans to take their VA dollars to other providers if they're not happy with the care they're getting from the Veterans Administration. He would increase competition throughout the system. For example, he would allow re-importation of drugs from Canada and elsewhere, and he would let people buy health insurance across state lines. But before I say too much, the point of the show is to let McCain describe his plan in his own words. McCain, like the other candidates we've featured, described his proposals at a forum in Washington organized by Families USA and the Federation of American Hospitals. Reach MD is bringing the highlights of that forum to you exclusively on XM Radio. All of the candidates were asked the same first question. Do you believe that all Americans should have health insurance coverage? And how would you make that happen? Here's what McCain said.
